x_1577958_dsb_pattern.name: ITOM Health: event management, AIOps and observability
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.overview: Ingest, reduce, bind, act. (1) Prefer OOB connectors (pull via MID) or the source tool's native push integration to the Event Management inbound endpoint; one integration per tool. (2) Event rules at the edge: ignore informational noise, normalise fields (node, type, resource, metric, message key), and set severity mapping. (3) CI binding by node name/IP/FQDN against a CMDB that follows the CMDB/CSDM pattern; unbound alerts are a data-quality signal, not an EM defect. (4) De-duplicate on message key, correlate with OOB tag-based and CMDB/service-based alert grouping (AIOps where licensed). (5) Alert management rules create incidents only for actionable, production, bound alerts, with service offering and support group from the CI; clearing policy agreed with the service desk. (6) Operator Workspace and service health for critical services. (7) Add remediation subflows for recurring alerts once stable. Measure compression and alert-to-incident ratios per source.
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.pain: Thousands of alerts a day across tools; genuine issues missed Duplicate tickets for the same outage Alerts without CI or service context, so impact is guessed Incidents raised manually and late; MTTR is high No single operations view across monitoring tools
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.summary: Monitoring tools each raise their own alerts; the operations team drowns in noise, duplicates are handled by hand, and incidents are raised late or without service context. The pattern converges on OOB Event Management: connectors or push integrations from each monitoring tool, event rules to filter and transform, CI binding to the CMDB, alert correlation and grouping, alert-to-incident rules with service impact, and Operator Workspace — measured by noise reduction and time to detect.
